scopeReview: PSO-4.A.1–2: independent states, nations, nation-states, stateless and multistate nations, multinational states and autonomous/semiautonomous regions. Contemporary Greenland and U.S. tribal governance examples verified against administering institutions. National identity is not inferred from biology, language or citizenship alone.
varietyReview: Cross-border settlement dot map, independent-entity comparison table, national-identity chart and nested autonomy map. Other items distinguish idealized nation-state alignment, collective/individual statelessness, scale-sensitive state terminology and evidence for national identity. Four stimuli, mixed keys/difficulty and all five skills.
repetitionReview: Distinct entity relationships rather than eleven synonym definitions. Two real governance examples concern different constitutional contexts, not interchangeable templates. No identical prompt or numerical clone; no assertion of empirical difficulty calibration.
referenceNote: Official curriculum and current primary government accounts checked in October2026. Most entities/data are explicitly hypothetical; no disputed state recognition is adjudicated, and the questions are geography education rather than individual legal advice. Sources remain in QA, not student resource imports. No human review claimed.

questions.correctOption: A multistate nation whose members live in more than one independent state.
questions.independentReview: Counted four R settlement dots west and four east of x50, with none on the boundary. Nation is explicitly self-identified rather than inferred from language or dots alone; sovereignty of A/B is supplied.

Independently compared each row’s governmental and external status rather than population size. Only A combines territorial government with external independence; no inference relies on international recognition disputes or a numerical threshold.

questions.correctOption: A multinational state, because more than one nation is present within its territory.
questions.independentReview: Confirmed mutually exclusive reported categories R70+S30=100 within one sovereign territory. The item explicitly supplies national identification and institutions instead of deriving nationhood from percentages or a language difference alone.

questions.correctOption: A boundary of a self-governing subnational region rather than evidence of full external independence.
questions.independentReview: Checked R polygon0–35 and remainder35–100 form one outer rectangle without a gap. Internal boundary x35 does not become an international frontier; allocated local powers and retained external affairs are explicitly supplied.

questions.correctOption: An autonomous political entity can exercise substantial local authority without being a separate independent state.
questions.independentReview: Verified current Danish Prime Minister’s Office descriptions and the Self-Government Act context. The question avoids claiming Greenland has no international activity or that every policy power remains with Denmark.

questions.correctOption: Tribal nations can possess distinct governmental authority within the U.S. political framework.
questions.independentReview: Checked BIA’s own status explanation. Did not claim every tribe has a reservation, every resident is a tribal member, or all tribal jurisdictions have identical powers; no specific legal dispute is assessed.

Verified the classification from explicitly supplied nation/sovereign-territory alignment, not a population-percentage cutoff. The explanation rejects an inference of genetic purity or absence of minorities.

questions.correctOption: The nation lacks its own independent state; that does not mean each person lacks citizenship.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished a national community’s lack of its own sovereign state from an individual’s citizenship. No contested real-world national claim or legal determination about a person is required.

questions.correctOption: The term can refer to an independent country or to a subnational unit, depending on scale and context.
questions.independentReview: Verified the scale/terminology distinction without treating all federal subdivisions worldwide as constitutionally identical. Fifty is the fixed current U.S. state count, not the number of territories or tribal governments.

questions.correctOption: Whether distinct self-identified national communities exist, rather than assuming language differences alone establish nations.
questions.independentReview: Checked that the requested classification concerns nations, not simply multilingualism. A single nation may use several languages and one language may be shared across several nations; neither is inferred from the supplied survey alone.

questions.correctOption: Citizenship data alone do not establish that all citizens share one national identity.
questions.independentReview: Compared the actual mapped variable, citizenship, with the caption’s stronger national-identity assertion. No cultural identity is assigned from color, passport or place of residence alone.
